disclaimer: This guide compares general approaches to controlling autonomous-agent spending as of 2026. Every team's needs differ; evaluate against your own stack and risk tolerance.

approaches.name: Prompt / instruction limits
approaches.what: Tell the agent its budget in the system prompt ("don't spend over $100").
cons: Not enforced — the model can ignore, forget, or miscount
No hard stop before money moves

approaches.name: Framework-native caps
approaches.what: Use a framework's built-in limits (max iterations, token/step caps, tool-call limits) in LangChain, the OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI, etc.

approaches.name: Virtual cards / provider caps
approaches.what: Issue a virtual card (or set a provider spend cap) with a hard limit per agent.
pros: Hard money cap at the card
cons: Coarse — usually one limit, no per-merchant/category/velocity logic
Blocks are after-the-fact at authorization, not policy-aware pre-checks

approaches.name: Build your own policy service
approaches.what: Write and host your own pre-spend policy engine.
cons: You build & maintain rules, storage, audit, approvals
Slow to ship; easy to get edge cases wrong

approaches.name: Dedicated agent spend firewall (sipi.bot)
approaches.what: The agent calls a policy engine (evaluate_spend) BEFORE it pays; it returns APPROVED / BLOCKED / FLAGGED against your rules — velocity, merchant allow/block, category limits, approval thresholds — across every framework, with an audit trail and human approval for FLAGGED items.
pros: Enforced before the spend, in real money
One policy across all agents & frameworks (MCP / HTTP / CLI)
cons: Adds a sub-second call in the payment path

spokes.title: How to stop an AI agent from overspending
spokes.angle: The failure mode (an agent with a card and no hard limit) and the four things a real control needs: pre-spend enforcement, real-money limits, granular rules, and an audit trail.

spokes.title: Do you need a spend firewall for AI agents?
spokes.angle: A decision checklist: if your agent can move money, calls external paid APIs/x402, or runs unattended, prompt limits and token caps are not enough.

spokes.title: AI agent budget controls: best practices
spokes.angle: Set per-agent budgets, use velocity limits, allow/block by merchant, require human approval above a threshold, and keep an audit trail. Enforce before the spend, not after.
